blogs.title: When the MRI is Normal: Diagnosing Acute Neuro-Behçet's Without Parenchymal Lesions
blogs.description: This post challenges the dogma that acute Neuro-Behçet's disease (NBD) always requires visible brainstem or basal ganglia lesions on MRI. Using a case of concurrent systemic and neurological Behçet's with a normal scan, we explore the entity of 'acute meningoencephalitic' NBD. We will review how to differentiate this from viral meningitis when CSF shows aseptic pleocytosis but imaging is unrevealing, emphasizing the critical role of mucocutaneous clues (oral/genital ulcers) in making the diagnosis before irreversible damage occurs.

blogs.title: Beyond the Usual Suspects: SIADH as a Primary Manifestation of CNS Vasculitis
blogs.description: Hyponatremia in the febrile patient often triggers a workup for pneumonia, malignancy, or drug toxicity. This article highlights a rare but crucial etiology: Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone (SIADH) driven purely by CNS inflammation in acute Neuro-Behçet's. We will dissect the pathophysiology linking IL-6 mediated neuroinflammation to ADH dysregulation and discuss why recognizing this association can prevent unnecessary extensive malignancy screenings and guide targeted anti-inflammatory therapy.

blogs.title: The Hiccuping Hyponatremic Patient: Connecting Persistent Hiccups, Rhabdomyolysis, and Sodium
blogs.description: Persistent hiccups and elevated CK are often dismissed as nonspecific symptoms of viral illness or dehydration. This post uses a clinical case to illustrate how these can be sentinel signs of severe hyponatremia secondary to SIADH. We will analyze the physiological mechanisms linking profound hyponatremia to intractable hiccups (central irritation) and rhabdomyolysis, urging clinicians to view these seemingly disconnected findings as a unified electrolyte emergency requiring urgent correction and source control.

blogs.title: Colchicine Monotherapy for Acute Neuro-Behçet's: Breaking the Steroid Reflex?
blogs.description: High-dose corticosteroids are the undisputed first-line treatment for acute Neuro-Behçet's, yet they carry significant morbidity. This post examines a controversial outlier case where colchicine monotherapy successfully resolved acute neurological symptoms, SIADH, and mucocutaneous lesions without steroids. We will weigh the evidence regarding colchicine's efficacy in parenchymal vs. non-parenchymal NBD, discuss its mechanism via IL-1β and IL-6 suppression, and propose scenarios where steroid-sparing strategies might be considered in resource-limited settings or specific patient phenotypes.

blogs.title: The Diagnostic Trap: Avoiding the 'Shotgun Approach' in Fever of Unknown Origin with Hyponatremia
blogs.description: In complex cases presenting with fever, headache, and hyponatremia, there is a tendency to order broad panels for sarcoidosis, lymphoma, and obscure infections immediately. Drawing from a case of Behçet's disease, this educational piece argues for a disciplined, step-wise diagnostic approach. We will discuss how non-specific markers like mildly elevated sIL-2R or ACE can lead clinicians down rabbit holes, and reinforce the value of rigorous clinical scoring systems (ICBD criteria) over reflexive testing when classic mucocutaneous signs are present.
